Question: Do you have a dedicated information security staff or office?

Question: Use this area to share information about your environment that will assist those who are assessing your company's data security program.

Question: Are you offering a cloud-based product?

Question: Does your product or service have an interface?

Question: Are you providing consulting services?
Additional Information: Basecamp is a self-serve SaaS product; 37signals does not sell implementation or consulting services as part of this offering.

Question: Does your solution have AI features, or are there plans to implement AI features in the next 12 months?
Additional Information: Basecamp does not include an AI assistant or AI features of any kind, and 37signals does not use AI with customer data; were that to change, it would be disclosed in the Privacy Policy. Disclosed alongside the No so it is not read as a denial: Basecamp supports Bring-Your-Own-Agent (BYOA) — a customer may connect their own AI agent to their own account through the Basecamp CLI and MCP servers, under the customer's own credentials and the customer's own AI provider's terms; 37signals runs no models on customer content. The Anthropic and OpenAI entries on the Basecamp subprocessor list cover staff use of those tools in day-to-day work (coding, QA, etc.) as part of operating Basecamp; the list covers all processing 37signals may perform in operating the Service and does not imply in-product AI. Question: Does your solution process protected health information (PHI) or any data covered by the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)?

Question: Is the solution designed to process, store, or transmit credit card information?
Additional Information: Credit card data is submitted directly to 37signals' payment processor (Braintree) and does not touch 37signals servers. 37signals stores only the last 4 digits of the card number for invoicing and account history, plus the billing address for tax and fraud detection; it does not store, process, or transmit full cardholder data. 37signals submits a PCI self-assessment (SAQ A), as noted in the Security Overview.

Question: Does operating your solution require the institution to operate a physical or virtual appliance in their own environment or to provide inbound firewall exceptions to allow your employees to remotely administer systems in the institution's environment?
Additional Information: Basecamp is delivered entirely as multi-tenant SaaS over HTTPS; no on-premises component and no inbound firewall exceptions are required.

Question: Does your solution have access to personal or institutional data?
Additional Information: 37signals processes customer content and personal data to provide the Service, with narrow, permission-gated staff access. Per the Privacy Policy, no 37signals human looks at customer content except for limited purposes with the customer's express permission.

Question: Do you have a well-documented business continuity plan (BCP), with a clear owner, that is tested annually?*

Question: Do you have a well-documented disaster recovery plan (DRP), with a clear owner, that is tested annually?*
Additional Information: The question is conjunctive — a documented DRP with a clear owner AND annual testing — and the testing limb currently fails: recovery drills across diverse failure scenarios ran regularly through early 2024 and have lapsed since (internally attested 2026-09-01; restart pending). The documented DR capability stands, owned by the Operations and SIP teams under the Business Continuity & Operational Resilience Policy (P-03, adopted 2026-08-31, reviewed at least annually or upon significant change): hourly database backups, automatic file backups on upload, and off-site backup storage. The answer returns to Yes when annual testing resumes.

Question: Have you undergone a SSAE 18/SOC 2 audit?
Additional Information: 37signals LLC has not completed a SOC 2 (SSAE 18) audit and has no current plans to pursue one. SOC reports for the third-party data-center facilities used are available under NDA. See the Security Overview.

Question: Do you conform with a specific industry standard security framework (e.g., NIST Cybersecurity Framework, CIS Controls, ISO 27001, etc.)?

See the Security Overview.

Question: Can you provide overall system and/or application architecture diagrams, including a full description of the data flow for all components of the system?

Question: Does your organization have a data privacy policy?

Question: Do you have a documented, and currently implemented, employee onboarding and offboarding policy?

Question: Do you perform security assessments of third-party companies with which you share data (e.g., hosting providers, cloud services, PaaS, IaaS, SaaS)?*
Additional Information: There is no formal, documented third-party security-assessment program prior to onboarding subprocessors. All subprocessors are bound by written data-processing agreements requiring protections no less protective than 37signals' own DPA.

Question: Do you have contractual language in place with third parties governing access to institutional data?*
Additional Information: Under the DPA, 37signals contractually requires every subprocessor to sign a written agreement with data-protection obligations at least as protective as 37signals' own DPA, including confidentiality, security, and access-limitation terms. This is a flow-down assurance to customers rather than a document the requesting institution can inspect directly — the underlying subprocessor contracts are private; summarized or certified copies are available on request per the DPA.

Question: Do the contracts in place with these third parties address liability in the event of a data breach?*
Additional Information: The customer-facing DPA's liability terms govern 37signals' own liability to the customer, not the terms of private subprocessor agreements. Subprocessor-contract liability language is not publicly published.

Question: Do you have an implemented third-party management strategy?*
Additional Information: Governed by the Supply Chain / Subprocessor Risk Management Policy (P-12, adopted 2026-08-31, reviewed at least annually or upon significant change): subprocessors are bound by DPA flow-down terms no less protective than 37signals' own DPA, the subprocessor list is published per product, and customers receive advance notice of subprocessor changes with a 10-business-day objection window and may subscribe to change notifications. No formal vendor-tiering scheme is published.

Question: Do you have a process and implemented procedures for managing your hardware supply chain (e.g., telecommunications equipment, export licensing, computing devices)?

Employee Macs are centrally managed via Iru (formerly Kandji) MDM and the Omarchy Linux workstations are managed separately, outside MDM, but no formal hardware supply-chain or export-licensing procedure is published.

Question: Will the institution be notified of major changes to your environment that could impact the institution's security posture?*

Question: Does the system support client customizations from one release to another?*
Additional Information: Basecamp is a single, standardized multi-tenant SaaS product, not per-customer-forked or on-premises. Account-level configuration is retained automatically across the continuous release process; there is no customer-specific code customization to lose.

Question: Do you have an implemented system configuration management process (e.g., secure "gold" images, etc.)?*
Additional Information: Production systems are provisioned and configured through automated configuration-management tooling to a standard secure configuration expressed as version-controlled code, with changes to that baseline made by the Operations team as code in version control, with attributed history. The process is set out in the Change-Management & Hardening-Baseline Policy, a written policy adopted 2026-08-31 and available on request. The baseline contents are held internal and available to assessors under NDA, and a standalone production-baseline document with a scheduled review is not yet produced. Company Macs run a standard configuration applied by Iru (formerly Kandji) MDM and are audited daily by Shipshape; the Omarchy Linux workstations run full-disk encryption and are managed separately, outside MDM.

Question: Do you have a documented change management process?
Additional Information: The Change-Management & Hardening-Baseline Policy, a written policy adopted 2026-08-31 and available on request, documents the process: every code and infrastructure change is version-controlled with attributed history; every change to Basecamp's main branch requires a passing CI sign-off, in which the engineer runs the test suites, static security analysis and dependency audits and the pass is recorded on the commit as an attributed status the main branch requires (repository administrators can bypass the check); production deploys run only from the main branch; changes can be validated on staging/beta; and production releases health-check before traffic cutover, with inherent rollback. Changes are made by a small team of senior engineers, with peer review where judgment calls for it. Infrastructure configuration is changed by the Operations team as code in version control, outside the CI sign-off.

Question: Does your change management process minimally include authorization, impact analysis, testing, and validation before moving changes to production?
Additional Information: The Change-Management & Hardening-Baseline Policy (a written policy, available on request) documents the testing and validation steps: changes to Basecamp's main branch pass the required CI sign-off before the branch accepts them (see CHNG-04), production deploys run only from the main branch, changes can be exercised on staging/beta, and the new version is health-checked before traffic cuts over. On Basecamp the required sign-off is the approval gate, with peer review where judgment calls for it. Infrastructure changes are made by the Operations team without a separate approval step, and no change carries a documented impact analysis, so the impact-analysis part of the question is not met, and the authorization part is not met for infrastructure changes.

Question: Does your change management process verify that all required third-party libraries and dependencies are still supported with each major change?
Additional Information: Third-party libraries are declared in versioned manifests with pinned lockfiles and updated through the change process, and the CI sign-off runs dependency audits for known vulnerabilities (Change-Management & Hardening-Baseline Policy, available on request). No step checks that a library is still supported.

Question: Do you have policy and procedure, currently implemented, managing how critical patches are applied to all systems and applications?

Question: Have you implemented policies and procedures that guide how security risks are mitigated until patches can be applied?

Question: Do clients have the option to not participate in or postpone an upgrade to a new release?

Question: Do you have a fully implemented solution support strategy that defines how many concurrent versions you support?

Question: Do you have a release schedule for product updates?

Question: Can solution updates be completed without institutional involvement (i.e., technically or organizationally)?

Question: Are upgrades or system changes installed during off-peak hours or in a manner that does not impact the customer?

Question: Do procedures exist to provide that emergency changes are documented and authorized (including after-the-fact approval)?
Additional Information: The Change-Management & Hardening-Baseline Policy, a written policy adopted 2026-08-31 and available on request, documents emergency changes: urgent fixes ship through the same version-controlled path and receive after-the-fact review, and they remain documented and attributed in the commit history and, for application deploys, the deploy audit log. The Change & Configuration Management Policy (P-04) adds that they are deployed under on-call authority and that the exception is recorded through the documented policy-exception process.

Question: Do you have a systems management and configuration strategy that encompasses servers, appliances, cloud services, applications, and mobile devices (company and employee owned)?

Question: Is your company subject to the institution's geographic region's laws and regulations?*

Question: Do you have a documented systems development life cycle (SDLC)?
Additional Information: 37signals publicly documents its product development methodology, Shape Up (six-week shaping/betting/building cycles, hill-chart progress tracking, cool-down periods), which is the process used to build and ship Basecamp itself. Question: Do you perform background screenings or multi-state background checks on all employees prior to their first day of work?

Question: Do you require new employees to fill out agreements and review policies?

Question: Do you have a documented information security policy?
Additional Information: Security practices are documented in the published Security Overview, which the DPA formally incorporates by reference as the Security, Privacy and Architecture Documentation governing 37signals' technical and organizational measures. This is an externally facing document rather than an internal ISMS policy with version history; if a review requires the latter specifically, security@37signals.com can discuss additional internal documentation shareable under NDA.

Question: Are information security principles designed into the product lifecycle?
Additional Information: Code changes to Basecamp pass automated security checks (Brakeman static analysis and dependency audits) in the required CI sign-off (see CHNG-04), and are peer-reviewed for security best practices, including OWASP guidance, where judgment calls for it. Newer applications including Basecamp use field-level "encryption at-work," where each database field is individually encrypted so engineers can operate and support the product without being exposed to customer content. See the Security Overview.

Question: Will you comply with applicable breach notification laws?
Additional Information: 37signals commits contractually (DPA) to notify customers without undue delay, and in compliance with applicable data protection law, after becoming aware of a Personal Data Incident. Separately, the Security Overview — which the DPA incorporates by reference — commits to contacting the account owner within 24 hours of an incident and working with the customer throughout.

Question: Do you have an information security awareness program?
Additional Information: Everyone at 37signals is trained and made aware of security concerns and best practices relevant to their systems and role. See the Security Overview.

Question: Is security awareness training mandatory for all employees?
Additional Information: Published materials describe this as a universal practice (everybody is trained) rather than using the specific word "mandatory"; completion-tracking and attestation records for this training are not published. See the Security Overview.

Question: Do you have process and procedure(s) documented, and currently followed, that require a review and update of the access list(s) for privileged accounts?
Additional Information: No scheduled review of privileged-account access lists is documented or run: staff access changes on joiner, mover and leaver events under the Identity & Access Management Policy, and there is no periodic review of the staff identity roster and no revalidation of role entitlements (the published CAIQ answers IAM-03.1 and IAM-08.1 Partial for this reason). What does run is narrower: all employee access to customer data is recorded per session and audited bi-weekly by the Security team using open-source access-auditing tools (console1984 and audits1984, per the Security Overview). That audit reviews how access was used, not who holds it. Admin access is limited need-to-know over VPN with 2FA.

Question: Do you have documented, and currently implemented, internal audit processes and procedures?
Additional Information: Scoped: a documented, recurring internal audit of employee access to customer data runs bi-weekly using console1984 and audits1984. 37signals does not maintain a broader enterprise internal-audit function (financial/operational); it is a privately held company without a dedicated internal-audit department.

Question: Does your organization have physical security controls and policies in place?
Additional Information: 37signals is a fully remote company with no corporate office housing customer data. Production infrastructure runs in third-party data centers with biometric access locks, round-the-clock interior and exterior surveillance, and 24/7/365 onsite staff; only authorized personnel have access. That evidence covers Chicago and Ashburn. Neither outpost is equivalently evidenced: the San Jose outpost is at Evocative SJC11 in Santa Clara, which is outside the provider's SOC 2, and the provider's management of the 37signals installation at Amsterdam is not attested — the same limit stated at DCTR-04 and DCTR-10. See the Security Overview.

Question: Does your solution support single sign-on (SSO) protocols for user and administrator authentication?*
Additional Information: Basecamp does not support SSO or SAML-based single sign-on. Users authenticate with an email address and password, or by signing in with a Google account.

Question: For customers not using SSO, does your solution support local authentication protocols for user and administrator authentication?*
Additional Information: All Basecamp authentication is local: email/password, or Sign in with Google. Since Basecamp has no SSO/SAML option, local authentication is the method available to every customer.

Question: For customers not using SSO, can you enforce password/passphrase complexity requirements (provided by the institution)?*
Additional Information: There is no mechanism for a customer to impose its own password policy; Basecamp enforces one fixed, vendor-defined policy for all accounts, consistent with the absence of SSO and directory integration.

Question: For customers not using SSO, does the system have password complexity or length limitations and/or restrictions?*
Additional Information: Passwords must be at least 12 characters, must not match the username/email, and must not appear in known-breach corpora (screened against Have I Been Pwned via a k-anonymity range query). There is no character-composition requirement (no mandated numbers or symbols); strength rests on length plus breach screening. Passwords are stored BCrypt-hashed.

Question: For customers not using SSO, do you have documented password/passphrase reset procedures that are currently implemented in the system and/or customer support?*
Additional Information: Self-service password reset via emailed link; account owners and admins can trigger a reset email for any team member from Adminland.

Question: Does your organization participate in InCommon or another eduGAIN-affiliated trust federation?*
Additional Information: Follows directly from Basecamp having no SAML/SSO support.

Question: Are there any passwords/passphrases hard-coded into your systems or solutions?*
Additional Information: No passwords or passphrases are hard-coded into systems or solutions.

Question: Are you storing any passwords in plaintext?*
Additional Information: All passwords are hashed and salted using BCrypt (cost factor 10); plaintext passwords are never stored, as documented in the Security Overview.

Question: Are audit logs available that include AT LEAST all of the following: login, logout, actions performed, and source IP address?*
Additional Information: Audit logs covering all four elements exist and are held by 37signals: login events are logged with IP address, browser, OS, and timestamp — surfaced to users, with new-device email notification and per-user login history; 37signals logs all access to all accounts by IP address; and centralized off-host server-side request logging records in-app actions performed with source IP, used by the Security team for its own operations. In-app activity timelines additionally record actions performed per person. There is no single customer-admin-facing, account-wide view combining these — the combined logs are vendor-held, with the per-user login history as the customer-visible slice.

Question: Describe or provide a reference to the (a) system capability to log security/authorization changes, as well as user and administrator security events (i.e., physical or electronic), such as login failures, access denied, changes accepted; and (b) all requirements necessary to implement logging and monitoring on the system. Include (c) information about SIEM/log collector usage.*
Additional Information: 37signals internally logs account access by IP address and audits internal employee access to customer data bi-weekly (console1984/audits1984 tooling), as described in the Security Overview. No customer-facing SIEM or log-collector integration is published or offered to customers.

Question: Can you provide the institution documentation regarding the retention period for those logs, how logs are protected, and whether they are accessible to the customer (and if so, how)?*
Additional Information: Documentation is available to assessors under NDA: central security/infrastructure logs are retained 30 days (retention enforced by the log platform), and privileged-console session records for Basecamp are incinerated after 30 days; log management is an Operations and SIP responsibility, and access to the log stores is restricted at the network level only, with no record kept of who reads them. These logs are internal and not accessible to customers.

Question: For customers not using SSO, does your application support integration with other authentication and authorization systems?
Additional Information: Basecamp has no SSO, SAML, or directory-integration support; no integration with external authentication or authorization systems is available.

Question: Do you allow the customer to specify attribute mappings for any needed information beyond a user identifier? (e.g., Reference eduPerson, ePPA/ePPN/ePE)
Additional Information: Not applicable in practice: no SSO/SAML integration exists to configure attribute mappings against.

Question: For customers not using SSO, does your application support directory integration for user accounts?
Additional Information: No LDAP, Active Directory, SCIM, or other directory-integration feature; accounts are created and managed manually inside Basecamp by owners and admins.

Question: Does your solution support any of the following web SSO standards: SAML2 (with redirect flow), OIDC, CAS, or other?
Additional Information: Basecamp supports none of these web SSO standards. Sign in with Google is a consumer convenience login (OAuth against the user's personal Google account), not an institution-controlled OIDC/SSO integration, and does not satisfy this requirement.

Question: Do you support differentiation between email address and user identifier?
Additional Information: A user's Basecamp login is their email address; no separate customer-facing or institution-configurable user identifier exists. Internally, 37signals maintains a single cross-product 37signals ID per person spanning multiple accounts, but it is not institution-visible or configurable.

Question: For customers not using SSO, does your application and/or user frontend/portal support multifactor authentication (e.g., Duo, Google Authenticator, OTP, etc.)?
Additional Information: Native two-factor authentication: a TOTP code from an authenticator app, with an option to add a hardware security key (USB key, fingerprint reader, Windows Hello). Account owners can require 2FA for all members from Adminland; admins can deactivate a locked-out member's 2FA on their behalf.

Question: Does your application automatically lock the session or log out an account after a period of inactivity?
Additional Information: No automatic inactivity timeout or session lock. Sessions persist via a browser cookie until manual logout (which signs out of all Basecamp accounts on that device) or until cookies are cleared.

Question: Will the institution's data be stored on any devices (database servers, file servers, SAN, NAS, etc.) configured with non-RFC 1918/4193 (i.e., publicly routable) IP addresses?*
Additional Information: Not publicly documented. Based on standard SaaS architecture, database and file storage servers would not be expected on publicly routable IPs — only edge/web-facing infrastructure — but this is not confirmed in published documentation.

Question: Is the transport of sensitive data encrypted using security protocols/algorithms (e.g., system-to-client)?*
Additional Information: Transport is encrypted with TLS 1.2/1.3 using ECDHE key exchange; modern clients negotiate TLS 1.3 with AES-256-GCM, and AEAD cipher suites are preferred (publicly verifiable via SSL Labs). A legacy TLS 1.2 CBC fallback (ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256) remains negotiable for older clients. The transport-cipher description in the published Security Overview (GeoTrust/RapidSSL certificates, AES_128_CBC) predates the current configuration; the published CAIQ (CEK-03.1) records the current state.

Question: Is the storage of sensitive data encrypted using security protocols/algorithms (e.g., disk encryption, at-rest, files, and within a running database)?*
Additional Information: Uploaded files are encrypted at rest using AES-256; backups are encrypted at rest at the storage layer using AES-256. Application databases are not encrypted at rest in the traditional disk-encryption sense; for Basecamp 5, 37signals instead uses field-level "encryption at-work" — every content field is encrypted with its own key, itself encrypted with a master key — so data stays encrypted while the database is actively serving requests. Passwords are hashed and salted with BCrypt and never stored recoverably. Note: the Security Overview states at-work encryption applies to HEY and Basecamp 5, while the Privacy Policy names HEY specifically; the Security Overview, as the more specific purpose-built document, is relied on here.

Question: Do all cryptographic modules in use in your solution conform to the Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS PUB 140-2 or 140-3)?*
Additional Information: No published claim of FIPS-validated cryptographic modules.

Question: Will the institution's data be available within the system for a period of time at the completion of this contract?*
Additional Information: Content becomes inaccessible via the live application immediately upon cancellation but is not immediately destroyed: contacting support can restore access within the first 30 days after cancellation. After 30 days, content is permanently deleted from active systems; backup copies are purged within 60 days, per the Terms of Service.

Question: Are ownership rights to all data, inputs, outputs, and metadata retained even through a provider acquisition or bankruptcy event?*
Additional Information: No contractual guarantee is published; the standard Terms of Service do not address acquisition- or bankruptcy-specific data rights.

Question: Do backups containing the institution's data ever leave the institution's data zone either physically or via network routing?*
Additional Information: Primary data centers are in Chicago, IL and Ashburn, VA, with read-only outposts in San Jose, CA and Amsterdam, Netherlands. Data does cross zones over the network: read-only database replicas reach both outposts. Backups themselves stay in the United States — outpost database hosts back up to the US storage arrays, and the outposts hold no object storage and no backup store. One backup class is outside that: the MySQL, Redis and miscellaneous sets are also synced to Cloudflare R2 object storage, which carries a location preference rather than an enforceable jurisdiction.

Question: Is media used for long-term retention of business data and archival purposes stored in a secure, environmentally protected area?*
Additional Information: The facility backup store sits in data centers physically secured with biometric locks, round-the-clock surveillance, restricted access, and 24/7/365 onsite staff, on the evidence described at DCTR-04, DCTR-09 and DCTR-11. One backup class is outside that evidence: the MySQL, Redis and miscellaneous sets synced to Cloudflare R2 (see DATA-07) sit on hardware Cloudflare operates, whose physical and environmental protection is Cloudflare's control, and no Cloudflare assurance report is held for it.

Question: At the completion of this contract, will data be returned to the institution and/or deleted from all your systems and archives?
Additional Information: Customers can export a full copy of their data before cancellation. After cancellation, content is permanently deleted from active systems within 30 days and from backups within 60 days; 37signals states it cannot recover data once permanently deleted.

Question: Can the institution extract a full or partial backup of data?
Additional Information: Account owners can export a full HTML copy of Basecamp data at any time — the entire account, a selection, or individual projects, including archived projects and Ping conversations. There is no native CSV or JSON export; the HTML export is designed for local viewing and backup rather than migration. Only account owners can access this feature.

Question: Do current backups include all operating system software, utilities, security software, application software, and data files necessary for recovery?
Additional Information: Hourly database backups and automatic file backups; disaster-recovery drills covering diverse disaster/failure scenarios were practiced regularly through early 2024 and have lapsed since (internally attested 2026-09-01; restart pending). Published material itemizes database and uploaded-file backups plus restoration testing; it does not separately itemize operating-system, utility, or security-software backup contents — recovery of those layers was exercised through the drills rather than evidenced as a backup-content inventory.

Question: Are you performing off-site backups (i.e., digitally moved off site)?
Additional Information: Backups are stored off-site for a maximum of 30 days.

Question: Are physical backups taken off-site (i.e., physically moved off site)?
Additional Information: No physical backup media exist to move: the published backup process is digital, network-based off-site storage of backups encrypted at rest across redundant data centers, with no physical media transported off-site. On pre-4.1.5 workbooks, whose dropdown offers only Yes/No on this row, the answer is No — the position is identical.

Question: Are data backups encrypted?
Additional Information: Backups of customer data are encrypted at rest at the storage layer: AES-256 on our own storage, and AES-256-GCM with our cloud storage provider, which backups reach over TLS. No additional application-level encryption is applied, and between the two primary data centers backups travel over dedicated private circuits without encryption in transit.

Question: Do you have a media handling process that is documented and currently implemented that meets established business needs and regulatory requirements, including end-of-life, repurposing, and data-sanitization procedures?
Additional Information: The Media Sanitization & Secure-Disposal Standard (adopted 2026-08-31, reviewed annually and on significant change) requires that storage media that held customer or personal data be sanitized or physically destroyed per NIST SP 800-88 before disposal, reuse, or return, with the same requirement flowing down to the colocation provider; managed staff devices are remote-wiped on loss or decommission. The standalone written operational procedure and records mechanism are provisional pending internal operational confirmation.

Question: Does the process described in DATA-15 adhere to DoD 5220.22-M and/or NIST SP 800-88 standards?
Additional Information: The Media Sanitization & Secure-Disposal Standard specifies NIST SP 800-88 (purge/clear methods that render recovery infeasible, or physical destruction). DoD 5220.22-M is not referenced. The specific technique per media type and the sanitization records are held internally, available under NDA.

Question: Does your staff (or third party) have access to institutional data (e.g., financial, PHI, or other sensitive information) through any means?
Additional Information: Staff can access customer data for support purposes only with the customer's express consent requested in advance; staff do not access data as a matter of course. Field-level encryption at-work (Basecamp 5) limits what engineers and admins can see during internal operations, and all employee access is audited bi-weekly (console1984/audits1984). See DATA-03 for the note on the documented scope of at-work encryption.

Question: Do you have a documented and currently implemented strategy for securing employee workstations when they work remotely (i.e., not in a trusted computing environment)?
Additional Information: Employee Mac computers are centrally managed via Iru (formerly Kandji) (disk encryption, firewall, password rules, app updates, remote wipe). VPN with two-factor authentication is required for internal server access. The Omarchy Linux workstations are managed separately, outside MDM: they run full-disk encryption but have no remote-wipe channel and no enforced automatic screen lock. All computers are hardened and audited daily via Shipshape.

Question: Does the environment provide for dedicated single-tenant capabilities? If not, describe how your solution or environment separates data from different customers (e.g., logically, physically, single tenancy, multi-tenancy).
Additional Information: No dedicated single-tenant deployment option is available; Basecamp is offered exclusively as multi-tenant SaaS. Each customer's data lives in its own logically scoped account within shared application and database infrastructure.

Question: Are ownership rights to all data, inputs, outputs, and metadata retained by the institution?
Additional Information: All materials submitted to the service remain the customer's property; 37signals is granted only a limited license to use submitted content to operate the service, per the Terms of Service.

Question: In the event of imminent bankruptcy, closing of business, or retirement of service, will you provide 90 days for customers to get their data out of the system and migrate applications?
Additional Information: No published commitment to a specific notice period exists in the standard Terms of Service or Privacy Policy.

Question: Are involatile backup copies made according to predefined schedules and securely stored and protected?
Additional Information: Database backups run hourly and files are backed up automatically on upload. Backups are encrypted at rest at the storage layer (AES-256) and stored off-site for up to 30 days. Our production MySQL databases are restored from backup monthly to refresh staging; backups of other datastores and the cloud copies are not covered by that restore testing.

Question: Do you have a cryptographic key management process (generation, exchange, storage, safeguards, use, vetting, and replacement) that is documented and currently implemented, for all system components (e.g., database, system, web, etc.)?
Additional Information: No single documented lifecycle process (generation, exchange, storage, vetting, replacement) covers all system components. Implemented practice: for Basecamp 5, every content field is encrypted with its own key (field-level encryption at-work); backups are encrypted at rest at the storage layer; TLS certificates and secrets are managed by the Operations and SIP teams under the Cryptography & Key Management Policy (P-05, adopted 2026-08-31). Rotation, custody, and replacement procedures are not yet documented end-to-end; the published CAIQ rates the corresponding controls Partial.

Question: Are access controls for institutional accounts based on structured rules, such as role-based access control (RBAC), attribute-based access control (ABAC), or policy-based access control (PBAC)?*
Additional Information: Basecamp account permissions are structured — owner and administrator roles, project-level access, and per-person visibility controls — consistent with role-based access control.

Question: Are you using a web application firewall (WAF)?*
Additional Information: Production Basecamp web traffic is fronted by Cloudflare with the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset and the OWASP Core Ruleset enabled on the production zones, plus zone rate limiting — a dedicated HTTP/application-layer WAF, distinct from the network-layer firewalls described in the Security Overview. Application-layer protection additionally includes framework-level defenses, an internally built anomaly-detection and auto-blocking system, and continuous external testing through the public HackerOne program.

Question: Are only currently supported operating system(s), software, and libraries leveraged by the system(s)/application(s) that will have access to institution's data?*
Additional Information: The software infrastructure is updated regularly with the latest security patches, per the Security Overview.

Question: Does your application require access to location or GPS data?*
Additional Information: Basecamp's mobile apps do not request GPS or location access; the Privacy Policy lists the device permissions the apps may request (contacts, calendar, camera, push notifications, file access), and location/GPS is not among them.

Question: Does your application provide separation of duties between security administration, system administration, and standard user functions?*
Additional Information: Dedicated Operations and SIP (security/infrastructure) teams are in charge of access and identity management, network connectivity, firewalls, and log file management, distinct from application-level user roles.

Question: Do you subject your code to static code analysis and/or static application security testing prior to release?*
Additional Information: Brakeman static analysis, failing on any warning, runs in the CI suite behind the required CI sign-off that changes to Basecamp's main branch pass (see CHNG-04). The SIP team reviews changes to code and infrastructure against best practices and security guidelines, including OWASP, where judgment calls for it.

Question: Do you have software testing processes (dynamic or static) that are established and followed?*
Additional Information: Automated tests and Brakeman static analysis run in the required CI sign-off on changes to Basecamp's main branch (see CHNG-04), with OWASP-aligned review where judgment calls for it; HEY and Basecamp 5 have also undergone security reviews and penetration tests performed by third-party security firms.

Question: Are access controls for staff within your organization based on structured rules, such as RBAC, ABAC, or PBAC?
Additional Information: Remote and administrative access to 37signals infrastructure is limited to staff who need it for their day-to-day work and requires two-factor authentication over VPN.

Question: Does the system provide data input validation and error messages?
Additional Information: As a mature production SaaS application subject to structured testing and static analysis, Basecamp performs data input validation and returns application error messages; this practice is not separately documented in a public statement.

Question: Do you have a process and implemented procedures for managing your software supply chain (e.g., libraries, repositories, frameworks, etc.)?
Additional Information: 37signals follows a documented engineering philosophy of minimizing third-party dependencies and manages its Ruby and JavaScript dependency surface through standard tooling; dependency audits (bundler-audit and importmap audit) run in the required CI sign-off on changes to Basecamp's main branch (see CHNG-04).

Question: Have your developers been trained in secure coding techniques?
Additional Information: All 37signals workers are trained and made aware of security concerns and best practices.

Question: Was your application developed using secure coding techniques?
Additional Information: Development follows OWASP-aligned review practices, static analysis, and third-party penetration testing.

Question: If mobile, is the application available from a trusted source (e.g., App Store, Google Play Store)?
Additional Information: The current Basecamp mobile app (Basecamp — Project Management) is distributed exclusively through the Apple App Store and Google Play Store.

Question: Do you have a fully implemented policy or procedure that details how your employees obtain administrator access to institutional instance of the application?
Additional Information: Employee access to customer data in Basecamp is access-controlled and independently audited on a bi-weekly cadence using the console1984 and audits1984 tooling.

Question: Select your hosting option.
Additional Information: A combination of two hosting models, which is the case the template directs to Other. 37signals owns and operates its own server hardware in leased colocation space at Summit (formerly Deft) facilities in Chicago, IL, Ashburn, VA and San Jose, CA. At the Amsterdam, Netherlands outpost the dedicated servers are the provider's own, maintained and operated by the provider, with 37signals nodes running as virtual machines on them. Neither model is public cloud, private cloud, nor traditional on-premise. One qualification, so this is not read as a categorical denial of cloud use: the MySQL, Redis and miscellaneous backup sets are synced to Cloudflare R2 object storage, which is public-cloud storage, and no production compute or primary datastore runs there — see DATA-07, DCTR-15 and DCTR-16.

Question: Is a SOC 2 Type 2 report available for the hosting environment?
Additional Information: For the primary facilities' physical-security controls: the colocation provider, Summit (formerly Deft), issues an annual SOC 2 Type II report (current cycle July 2025–June 2026, unqualified opinion, Security criteria only; earlier cycles also carried Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality and Privacy, and Summit has committed to reintroduce Availability in its FY2027 report). At Chicago and Ashburn the physical-security controls are the facility operators' own, carried in the report under the carve-out method: described rather than tested by Summit's auditor, whose testing covers Summit's monitoring of those operators. Neither outpost is evidenced on that basis: the San Jose outpost's facility, Evocative SJC11 in Santa Clara, is not a subservice organization in the report at all, and the Amsterdam outpost runs on Summit's own dedicated servers, whose coverage by the facility operator's controls is inferred rather than attested (see DCTR-09). The SOC 2 can be shared under an NDA or confidentiality terms comparable to Summit's with 37signals; Summit's SOC 3 for the same system and period can be shared without one, including with prospective customers, and carries the auditor's opinion and the system description without control-testing detail or test results. Summit reports that each facility operator holds its own SOC 2 Type 2 covering environmental controls; 37signals has requested those reports and has not yet verified Summit's account against them, so none is available from us. 37signals LLC itself has not completed a SOC audit; application- and organization-layer controls are addressed by 37signals' own published security program.

Question: Are you generally able to accommodate storing each institution's data within its geographic region?
Additional Information: Per-institution geographic data placement is not offered. Data sits on a fixed four-facility footprint — Chicago, IL; Ashburn, VA; San Jose, CA; and Amsterdam, Netherlands — and placement is not selectable by institution or region. The read-write primary, the object store holding uploaded files and the facility backup store are in the US primaries; the outposts hold read-only replicas. One backup class sits outside that footprint: the MySQL, Redis and miscellaneous sets are also synced to Cloudflare R2 object storage, which carries a location preference rather than an enforceable jurisdiction (see DATA-07), so it cannot be placed in an institution's region either.

Question: Are the data centers staffed 24 hours a day, seven days a week (i.e., 24 x 7 x 365)?
Additional Information: Chicago and Ashburn have 24/7/365 onsite staff. Neither outpost is equivalently evidenced: the San Jose outpost is at Evocative SJC11 in Santa Clara, which is outside the provider's SOC 2, and staffing evidence was never gathered for Amsterdam. The answer rests on the two primary facilities rather than on all four, the same limit stated at DCTR-10 and DCTR-11.

Question: Are your servers separated from other companies via a physical barrier, such as a cage or hard walls?
Additional Information: 37signals equipment occupies dedicated cabinets, and the Ashburn facility documents crash-rated, anti-climb cages with dual-factor biometric and proximity access control. Ashburn is the only site with cage evidence on file; Chicago and San Jose are not separately evidenced for it, and that is a site-evidence gap rather than something the outposts share. Amsterdam is different in kind: 37signals owns no servers there, because every node at that outpost is a virtual machine on the provider's own dedicated hardware, so there is no 37signals physical estate to enclose and the separation that applies is logical rather than a cage.

Question: Does a physical barrier fully enclose the physical space, preventing unauthorized physical contact with any of your devices?*
Additional Information: Facilities use biometric locks, round-the-clock surveillance, and authorized-personnel-only access; Ashburn cages are crash-rated and anti-climb. Summit's current SOC 2 Type II report, available on request, substantiates the physical controls at the facility level. Ashburn is the only site with enclosure evidence on file, on the same footing as DCTR-05, and at Amsterdam the enclosed devices would be the provider's own servers rather than 37signals equipment.

Question: Are your primary and secondary data centers geographically diverse?
Additional Information: The facilities are in Ashburn, VA and Chicago, IL — roughly 700 miles apart, in different regions and power grids.

Question: Is the service hosted in a high-availability environment?
Additional Information: Basecamp runs active/active across both data centers using BGP Anycast; other critical applications run active/standby with failover capability.

Question: Is redundant power available for all data centers where institutional data will reside?
Additional Information: Redundant power is documented at all four facilities by published facility specifications. Chicago (Digital Realty CH1, Elk Grove Village, Illinois): N+2 UPS redundancy. Ashburn (Digital Realty IAD24): 2N UPS redundancy and 12,000 kW generator capacity. San Jose read-only outpost (Evocative SJC11, Santa Clara, managed by Summit): N+1 UPS, four 1.5 MW generators and dual utility feeds from diverse substations. Amsterdam read-only outpost (Equinix AM1): N+1 UPS and N+1 standby power. These are the facilities' published specifications, not audited results. Summit's SOC 2 Type II does not reach San Jose, because Evocative is not a subservice organization in it, and its coverage of our Amsterdam installation (Summit's own dedicated servers at a facility on its list) is not established. Testing of redundant power at the outposts is not evidenced (see DCTR-10).

Question: Are redundant power strategies tested?*
Additional Information: Redundant power is in place, but testing at planned intervals is not evidenced for the current report cycle. The prior cycle of Summit's SOC 2 Type II report carried, as facility operators' controls described rather than tested by Summit's auditor, that generators are tested annually, that third-party preventive maintenance inspections of the generators run annually, and that third-party specialists inspect power-management systems on a predefined maintenance schedule, with UPS units covering temporary loss or surge. The current, Security-only report no longer carries those test-cadence controls; it states that every subservice facility is fully equipped with redundant UPS, backup generators and cooling, with proactive maintenance on critical systems a facility-selection standard. Neither outpost is equivalently evidenced: Amsterdam until the 37signals installation there is attested, and San Jose because its facility, Evocative SJC11, is outside Summit's SOC 2 (see DCTR-09). Summit reports that the facility operators' own SOC 2 reports cover inspection, maintenance and testing of power systems at each site, though without a stated load-test frequency at Chicago and Ashburn; 37signals has requested those reports and has not yet verified Summit's account against them, so this answer does not rest on it. It changes when the reports show testing at planned intervals at every site.

Question: Does the center where the data will reside have cooling and fire-suppression systems that are active and regularly tested?
Additional Information: Cooling and fire suppression are in place, but regular testing is not evidenced for the current report cycle. Cooling is N+1 at both Chicago and Ashburn. The prior cycle of Summit's SOC 2 Type II report carried, as a complementary subservice-organization control, that fire detection and suppression equipment is in place at each data center with third-party specialists inspecting those systems annually; that is the facility operators' control, described in the report rather than tested by Summit's auditor. The current, Security-only report does not re-attest the inspection cadence; it lists environmental and fire protection systems and redundant HVAC among the standards every subservice facility meets. Neither outpost is covered: the San Jose outpost is at Evocative SJC11 in Santa Clara, which is not a facility on Summit's subservice list (see DCTR-09), and Summit's management of the 37signals installation at Amsterdam is not attested. Summit reports that the facility operators' own SOC 2 reports cover maintenance and testing of cooling and fire protection at each site; 37signals has requested those reports and has not yet verified Summit's account against them, so this answer does not rest on it.

Question: Do you have Internet Service Provider (ISP) redundancy?
Additional Information: For the primary datacenters: each has external connections to the internet, to the other datacenter and to AWS, each over diverse physical paths. The San Jose and Amsterdam outposts are not evidenced for provider redundancy and sit in the same open network limb as DCTR-13; San Jose has no physical inter-datacenter circuit and reaches the rest of the fleet over the internal network backbone.

Question: Does every data center where the institution's data will reside have multiple telephone company or network provider entrances to the facility?
Additional Information: The question asks about every data center, and multiple provider entrances are not evidenced at either outpost. Chicago (Digital Realty CH1): multiple major carriers are on site, per Digital Realty's facility page, which states no count of provider entrances or diverse paths. Ashburn has two diverse fiber paths and direct links to all major carriers and public cloud providers. The San Jose and Amsterdam outposts have no facility-specific carrier-entrance evidence on file: the material behind the Chicago and Ashburn answer covers those two sites only and was never in scope for either outpost.

Question: Do you require multifactor authentication for all administrative accounts in your environment?
Additional Information: Remote access to servers is via VPN with two-factor authentication, limited to workers who need it for their day-to-day work.

Question: Are you using your cloud provider's available hardening tools or pre-hardened images?
Additional Information: No cloud-provider-supplied hardening toolchain exists in the production stack, so 37signals hardens its own images and configuration directly. Chicago, Ashburn and San Jose run 37signals-owned hardware in colocation. Amsterdam runs on the provider's own dedicated servers, and the provider supplies no hardening images or toolchain there either: 37signals builds and hardens those guests itself. The one cloud data flow, the Cloudflare R2 backup sync described at DATA-07, is object storage with no compute image to harden.

Question: Does your cloud solution provider have access to your encryption keys?
Additional Information: No outside provider holds 37signals' encryption keys: keys for stored files and for Basecamp 5 database content are managed internally, held neither by the colocation provider nor by the provider that owns the Amsterdam servers. Production compute is not public cloud, but one cloud data flow exists, the Cloudflare R2 backup sync described at DATA-07. Cloudflare manages its own server-side encryption keys over the objects it stores; those protect its storage layer and are not 37signals' application or content keys.

Question: Are you utilizing a stateful packet inspection (SPI) firewall?*
Additional Information: Products run on a dedicated network secured with firewalls and carefully monitored, per the Security Overview.

Question: Do you have a documented policy for firewall change requests?*
Additional Information: The Network-Defense & Firewall/Network-Change Policy, a written policy adopted 2026-08-31 and available on request, documents how firewall and network-defense changes are made: by the Operations team, as code in version control with attributed history, applied to production only from the main branch, with drift checks comparing the live configuration with the repositories, and with every change logged and attributed. There is no separate approval step or change-request ticket; a change is authorized by the Operations engineer who makes it (see FIDP-06).

Question: Have you implemented an intrusion detection system (network-based)?*
Additional Information: 37signals operates an internally built system that monitors and automatically blocks suspicious network- and application-layer activity, including vulnerability scanning and failed-login patterns; this is a custom in-house system rather than a named commercial IDS product.

Question: Do you employ host-based intrusion detection?*
Additional Information: The intrusion monitoring system operates at the network/application-ingress layer; per-host IDS agents are not described in published material.

Question: Are audit logs available for all changes to the network, firewall, IDS, and IPS systems?*
Additional Information: Network, firewall and edge configuration is managed as code and changed by our Operations team in version control, whose history (who, when and what changed) is the change record and is kept indefinitely. The running configuration of every network device is also captured hourly, so a change made outside version control is still recorded, and daily drift checks alert when live configuration diverges from the repositories. Device logs, including configuration commits, are centralized and kept for 30 days. Detailed change logs are internal and available under NDA on request.

Question: Is authority for firewall change approval documented? Please list approver names or titles in Additional Info.
Additional Information: There is no separate approval step, so there is no approval authority to name: firewall and network changes are made by the Operations team as code in version control and applied to production from the main branch, a change is authorized by the Operations engineer who makes it, and every change is logged and attributed.

Question: Have you implemented an intrusion prevention system (network-based)?
Additional Information: The same internally built system both monitors and automatically blocks suspicious activity, providing prevention as well as detection; it is a custom in-house system rather than a named commercial IPS product.

Question: Do you employ host-based intrusion prevention?
Additional Information: As with host-based detection, the prevention capability operates at the network/application layer; per-host prevention agents are not described in published material.

Question: Are you employing any next-generation persistent threat (NGPT) monitoring?
Additional Information: Not addressed in published material; internal operational detail, available under NDA on request. The internally built automated monitoring and blocking system is the closest published capability but is not described as NGPT-class monitoring.

Question: Is intrusion monitoring performed internally or by a third-party service?
Additional Information: Intrusion monitoring is performed by 37signals' own internally built system, with alerts escalated to the dedicated Operations/SIP team for manual investigation.

Question: Do you monitor for intrusions on a 24 x 7 x 365 basis?
Additional Information: Automated monitoring and blocking run continuously by design, and 37signals commits to contacting affected account owners within 24 hours of an incident; an explicit 24x7x365 human-staffing claim is not separately published.

Question: Do you have a formal incident response plan?
Additional Information: The incident-response plan is documented in the Security Incident Response & Forensics Policy (P-11, adopted 2026-08-31, amended 2026-10-06 with an incident-response plan section, and available on request). P-11 records the plan 37signals runs: an internal incident-response playbook maintained in version control since 2019 — severity levels (Critical, Major), roles (an Incident Lead, a Customer Liaison from Customer Support, the Operations on-call as first responder, SIP leading security incidents), declaration, escalation and customer communication, with dedicated protocols for account compromise and data breach — and a dedicated internal incident project, in use since 2015, in which incidents are declared, coordinated and written up with their cause and remediation. P-11 also sets the commitment to contact affected account owners within 24 hours of an incident and the DPA's breach-notification obligation. The plan has not yet been exercised or formally evaluated; the published CAIQ rates those controls (SEF-04.1, SEF-07.2) Partial.

Question: Do you either have an internal incident response team or retain an external team?
Additional Information: Internal: dedicated internal Operations and SIP teams are responsible for incident response — the question is satisfied by an internal team.

Question: Do you have the capability to respond to incidents on a 24 x 7 x 365 basis?
Additional Information: 37signals maintains continuous automated monitoring with escalation to the Operations team and commits to contacting affected customers within 24 hours of an incident; an explicit published 24x7x365 staffing commitment is not available.

Question: Do you carry cyber-risk insurance to protect against unforeseen service outages, data that is lost or stolen, and security incidents?
Additional Information: 37signals does not carry cyber-risk insurance.

Question: Are your systems and applications scanned with an authenticated user account for vulnerabilities (that are remediated) prior to new releases?*
Additional Information: Consistent with the static application security testing and established testing processes applied prior to release; the authenticated-scanning practice is not separately documented in a public statement.

Question: Will you provide results of application and system vulnerability scans to the institution?*
Additional Information: Per-customer sharing of vulnerability scan results is not offered; the public HackerOne bug bounty program is the designated external-facing security testing channel.

Question: Will you allow the institution to perform its own vulnerability testing and/or scanning of your systems and/or application, provided that testing is performed at a mutually agreed upon time and date?*
Additional Information: External testing is channeled through the public HackerOne bug bounty program, the designated and controlled channel, rather than ad hoc institutional scanning.

Question: Have your systems and applications had a third-party security assessment completed in the last year?
Additional Information: 37signals has undergone third-party security reviews and penetration tests for HEY and Basecamp 5, and has run a continuous public HackerOne bug bounty program since October 2020 as an ongoing external testing channel; a specific date for the most recent formal third-party penetration test is not published.

Question: Do you regularly scan for common web application security vulnerabilities (e.g., SQL injection, XSS, XSRF, etc.)?
Additional Information: Static application security testing prior to release plus authenticated vulnerability scanning before new releases, supplemented by continuous crowdsourced testing through the public HackerOne bug bounty program.

Question: Are your systems and applications regularly scanned externally for vulnerabilities?
Additional Information: Continuously tested by external, independent security researchers through the public HackerOne bug bounty program since October 2020.

Additional Information: Per his public self-description, he leads quality and accessibility at Basecamp.

Question: Web Link to Accessibility Statement or VPAT
Additional Information: basecamp.com/accessibility is Basecamp's accessibility statement; 37signals.com/policies/accessibility carries the published Basecamp Accessibility Conformance Report (VPAT). See ITAC-06 on the ACR's report date.

Question: Has a VPAT or ACR been created or updated for the solution and version under consideration within the past 12 months?*
Additional Information: A formal Basecamp Accessibility Conformance Report (VPAT 2.4Rev International Edition) is published at 37signals.com/policies/accessibility (live 2026-08-31), but the report's own face reads "Report Date: June 2025 (Replaces VPAT 2.4 completed 08/2023)" — outside the trailing 12 months — and names Basecamp 4 as the product and version. Question: Will your company agree to meet your stated accessibility standard or WCAG 2.1 AA as part of your contractual agreement for the solution?*
Additional Information: 37signals is actively working toward WCAG 2.2 level AA and treats it as the target standard, but does not offer a contractual conformance warranty.

Question: Does the solution substantially conform to WCAG 2.1 AA?*
Additional Information: Qualified: Basecamp is designed and tested against WCAG 2.2 level AA guidelines (a superset of 2.1 AA) as an ongoing practice — new features are built with accessibility in mind, tested for keyboard operability and color contrast, and checked with the axe and Accessibility Insights browser extensions — but 37signals does not formally attest to full conformance, and the published Basecamp Accessibility Conformance Report (self-assessed, report-dated June 2025) records Partially Supports on several WCAG success criteria (e.g., 2.1.1 Keyboard, 1.4.2 Audio Control) rather than attesting substantial conformance. See 37signals.com/policies/accessibility.

Question: Do you have a documented and implemented process for reporting and tracking accessibility issues?*
Additional Information: Accessibility issues can be reported to accessibility@basecamp.com. Reports are tracked to resolution through our standard bug process, as bug cards on our on-call boards, owned by our Quality & Accessibility lead. Accessibility is checked during development with the axe and Accessibility Insights browser extensions, complemented by regular manual audits of shipped features.

Question: Do you have documentation to support the accessibility features of your solution?

Additional Information: Consistent with PRPO-09; with no fully automated decision-making in the product, no such management process is needed.

Question: Do you have a documented policy for sharing information with law enforcement?
Additional Information: The Privacy Policy states: "Our policy is to not respond to government requests for user data unless we are compelled by legal process or in limited circumstances in the event of an emergency request," and that data is provided only if U.S. law enforcement authorities have the necessary warrant, criminal subpoena, or court order.

Question: Do you share any institutional data with law enforcement without a valid warrant or subpoena?*
Additional Information: Policy is to not respond to government requests for user data unless compelled by a valid warrant, criminal subpoena, or court order. The one exception stated in the Privacy Policy's law-enforcement clause — limited emergency circumstances as described there — is disclosed alongside the No: it is the policy's own narrowly-scoped emergency provision, not a practice of warrantless sharing.

Question: Does your incident response team include a privacy analyst/officer?
Additional Information: Consistent with PCOM-04: 37signals has no dedicated privacy staff or office, so the incident response team does not include a designated privacy analyst/officer.

Question: Will data be collected from or processed in or stored in the European Economic Area (EEA)?
Additional Information: Data is collected from EEA data subjects, and some of it is stored in the EEA. 37signals operates a facility in Amsterdam, Netherlands which holds read-only database replicas. The read-write primary database, the object store holding uploaded files and the facility backup store remain in the United States (Chicago, Ashburn), so EEA-originated data is still transferred to and processed in the US under the DPA and GDPR Standard Contractual Clauses (Modules 2/3). The Amsterdam presence adds EEA-resident read-only storage; it does not change the transfer position or the reliance on the Clauses.

Question: Do you have a data protection officer (DPO)?
Additional Information: 37signals has not published a formally designated Data Protection Officer. Privacy inquiries and DPA questions are directed to privacy@37signals.com (DPA §4.4 — a contact channel, not a DPO title). Consistent with PCOM-04 (no dedicated privacy staff/office).

Question: Will you sign appropriate GDPR Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) with the institution?
Additional Information: By signing the 37signals Agreement, the customer and 37signals are deemed to have executed the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (Module 2 controller-to-processor and Module 3 processor-to-processor, as applicable), with Irish law and the Irish Data Protection Commission as governing law and forum (DPA §11.2).

Question: Will data be collected from or processed in or stored in China?
Additional Information: No for everything 37signals can evidence, with classes it cannot exclude. No 37signals facility is in China (the facilities are Chicago, Ashburn, San Jose and Amsterdam), and no subprocessor on the published Basecamp list is based in China: each entry gives the country of the company 37signals contracts with, the United States for all except Birdie (France) and Plausible (Estonia). That country is the company's domicile, not a statement of where it processes data. Four flows have no established processing location, so this No does not exclude China for them: push notifications delivered through Apple Push Notification service and Google Firebase Cloud Messaging; the Cloudflare R2 backup class described at DATA-07, which carries a placement preference for eastern North America rather than an enforceable jurisdiction; customer avatar images, which are served through the CDN from edge locations we do not specify; and Plausible analytics on the signup and welcome pages, named on the Basecamp subprocessor list with Estonia, its contracting company's country, whose hosting in Germany is the vendor's own statement and has not been confirmed by 37signals. Nothing indicates China placement for any of them. Users may access Basecamp from anywhere, including China — content submitted by users located outside the United States is transferred to and stored in the United States per the Privacy Policy; 37signals imposes no geographic access restriction.

Question: Do you comply with PIPL security, privacy, and data localization requirements?
Additional Information: 37signals does not represent PIPL compliance, and no PIPL-related statement appears in any published material. This answer rests on that posture, not on a geographic exclusion: as INTL-04 records, the flows with no established processing location (push notifications, the R2 backups, the CDN-served avatars and Plausible analytics) mean China cannot be excluded for them.

Question: Have you performed a Data Privacy Impact Assessment for the solution/project?
Additional Information: No formal DPIA has been performed. In our assessment, 37signals' processing (SaaS project-management/collaboration content, determined entirely by the customer) does not appear to meet GDPR Art. 35 high-risk triggers (no systematic large-scale profiling, no large-scale special-category processing, no public-area monitoring) as a general matter — this is our own analysis, not a position 37signals has published. 37signals commits under its DPA (§2.3.5) to provide reasonable assistance if a customer needs to perform its own DPIA.

Question: Do you provide an end-user privacy notice about privacy policies and procedures that identify the purpose(s) for which personal information is collected, used, retained, and disclosed?
Additional Information: The Privacy Policy is structured around exactly this: what is collected and why, and how it is used, retained, and disclosed.

Question: Do you describe the choices available to the individual and obtain implicit or explicit consent with respect to the collection, use, and disclosure of personal information?
Additional Information: Mobile permissions are requested only with optional user consent, and cookie controls are described in the Privacy Policy.

Question: Do you collect personal information only for the purpose(s) identified in the agreement with an institution or, if there is none, the purpose(s) identified in the privacy notice?
Additional Information: The Privacy Policy's guiding principle is to collect only what is needed.

Question: Do you have a documented list of personal data your service maintains?
Additional Information: Described narratively in the Privacy Policy's "What we collect and why" section (identity/access, billing, product content, geolocation, analytics, cookies, correspondence, mobile permissions) rather than as a standalone itemized table.

Question: Do you retain personal information for only as long as necessary to fulfill the stated purpose(s) or as required by law or regulation and thereafter appropriately dispose of such information?
Additional Information: If an account is deleted, content is deleted within 60 days; deleted content is kept in an accessible trash for about 25 days and purged from all systems and logs within 90 days (Privacy Policy). This is consistent with the Security Overview's 30-day active/60-day backup figures once read as outer-bound vs. phased timelines.

Question: Do you provide individuals with access to their personal information for review and update (i.e., data subject rights)?
Additional Information: The Privacy Policy publishes a Right of Access and a Right to Correction; many rights can be exercised directly by signing in and updating account information.

Question: Do you disclose personal information to third parties only for the purpose(s) identified in the privacy notice or with the implicit or explicit consent of the individual?
Additional Information: With a caveat: 37signals never sells data and follows a subprocessor-only sharing model. One narrow exception exists (the ad-exclusion hash disclosure, see DRPV-13), and it is disclosed in the Privacy Policy itself.

Question: Do you protect personal information against unauthorized access (both physical and logical)?
Additional Information: VPN plus 2FA for system access, encryption in transit and at rest, at-work encryption for Basecamp 5, biometric-locked and 24/7-staffed data centers, and console1984/audits1984 access logging and auditing (Security Overview).

Question: Do you maintain accurate, complete, and relevant personal information for the purposes identified in the privacy notice?
Additional Information: Scoped: self-service mechanisms exist for individuals to review and correct their own information; accuracy of customer-controlled content is otherwise the customer's/data subject's responsibility per the DPA (§2.2.2).

Question: Do you have procedures to address privacy-related noncompliance complaints and disputes?
Additional Information: Data subjects have a published "Right to Complain," and privacy inquiries route to privacy@37signals.com (DPA §4.4). A detailed internal complaint-handling procedure is not separately published.

Question: Do you "anonymize," "de-identify," or otherwise mask personal data?
Additional Information: The Privacy Policy states: "We may aggregate and/or de-identify information collected through the services."

Question: Do you or your subprocessors use or disclose "anonymized," "de-identified," or otherwise masked data for any purpose other than those identified in the agreement with an institution (e.g., sharing with ad networks or data brokers, marketing, creation of profiles, analytics unrelated to services provided to institution)?
Additional Information: In one narrow, published respect: 37signals may disclose a one-way hash of a Basecamp account holder's email address to ad companies solely to exclude that person from seeing 37signals' own ads (suppression, not targeting or profiling). This applies to an institution's own Basecamp users' account emails, not merely to visitors of 37signals' marketing site; it does not touch Basecamp project content and is not a sale under the CCPA. Separately, 37signals states it may use de-identified or aggregated data "for any purpose, including marketing or analytics" (Privacy Policy).

Question: Do you certify stop-processing requests, including any data that is processed by a third party on your behalf?
Additional Information: Upon request: on termination, 37signals returns and (where legally permitted) deletes Personal Data per its published retention timelines; certification of deletion under the GDPR SCCs is provided only upon the customer's request, not automatically (DPA §8, §11.8).

Question: Do you have a process to review code for ethical considerations?
Additional Information: No public evidence of a formal ethics-in-code-review process.

Question: Does your service use AI for the processing of institutional data?
Additional Information: No in-product AI acts on customer data: Basecamp has no in-product AI, and 37signals does not use AI with customer data. The Anthropic/OpenAI entries on the Basecamp subprocessor list are staff day-to-day tooling that does not process customer content. Any AI processing of a customer's own data through bring-your-own-agent (BYOA) is performed by the customer's own agent, under the customer's own credentials and AI provider terms, outside 37signals' processing.

Question: Is any institutional data retained in AI processing?*
Additional Information: No institutional data enters any AI processing operated by 37signals (see DPAI-01), so none is retained in AI processing.

Question: Do you have agreements in place with third parties or subprocessors regarding the protection of customer data and use of AI?*
Additional Information: No in-product AI acts on customer data (see DPAI-01). For completeness: every subprocessor, the staff-tooling AI vendors included, is bound by a written agreement with data-protection obligations not less protective than the DPA (§5.1), and the AI vendors' commercial terms prohibit training on customer content.

Question: Will institutional data be processed through a third party or subprocessor that also uses AI?
Additional Information: No subprocessor processes institutional data on 37signals' behalf using AI; no in-product AI acts on customer data (see DPAI-01).

Question: Is AI processing limited to fully licensed commercial enterprise AI services?
Additional Information: No AI processing of institutional data occurs (see DPAI-01). Staff tooling uses the vendors' commercial services under click-through commercial terms (not negotiated agreements); no customer data is involved.

Question: Will institutional data be used or processed by any shared AI services?
Additional Information: No institutional data is used or processed by any shared AI services; no in-product AI acts on customer data (see DPAI-01).

Question: Do you have safeguards in place to protect institutional data and data privacy from unintended AI queries or processing?
Additional Information: No 37signals AI ingestion path exists to safeguard, since no in-product AI acts on customer data (see DPAI-01). The operating rule is that staff AI tooling is not used on customer data; separately, staff access to customer data is need-to-know, per-session consent-gated, and bi-weekly audited, which limits and detects access but is not claimed as a technical block on what an authorized person could paste into a tool — no DLP-style AI-ingestion control exists.

Question: Do you provide choice to the user to opt out of AI use?
Additional Information: There is no in-product AI use to opt out of (see DPAI-01). BYOA is entirely customer-initiated: nothing runs unless the customer connects an agent, and revoking the agent's credentials ends it.
